guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Centres performing aortic surgery are recommended to enter cases in a validated prospective registry to allow for monitoring of practice and outcomes.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Centres or networks of collaborating centres treating patients with abdominal aortic aneurysms should be able to provide both endovascular and open aortic surgery.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Centres performing abdominal aortic aneurysm repair should not have a yearly total caseload of < 30, and not less than 15 each by open and endovascular methods.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Centres treating complex abdominal aortic aneurysms should not have a yearly combined caseload of open and fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair of < 20.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Simulation based vascular surgery training curriculum should include open surgical repair and endovascular repair of AAA.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm who have reached the size threshold at which repair is considered should receive a fast track pathway\* to vascular surgical care.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Ultrasonography is recommended for the first line diagnosis and surveillance of small abdominal aortic aneurysms.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: The anteroposterior plane with consistent calliper placement should be considered the preferred method for ultrasound abdominal aortic diameter measurement.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Computed tomography angiography is recommended for treatment planning, once the aortoesophageal diameter threshold for elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair has been reached, in order to assess the risk of rupture.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Aortic diameter measurement with computed tomography angiography is recommended using dedicated post-processing software analysis; with consistent calliper placement in an orthogonal plane perpendicular to the aorta.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Ultrasound screening for the early detection of abdominal aortic aneurysm is recommended in high risk populations\* to reduce death from aneurysm rupture.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an incidentally detected abdominal aortic aneurysm should be referred to a vascular surgeon for evaluation, except for cases with very limited life expectancy.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Men should be considered for imaging surveillance using ultrasound, every five years for a sub-aneurysmal aorta 25 - 29 mm in diameter, every three years for abdominal aortic aneurysms 30 - 39 mm in diameter, annually for aneurysms 40-49 mm, and every six months for aneurysms >50 mm, taking into account life expectancy, suitability for future repair, and patient preferences.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Women should be considered for imaging surveillance using ultrasound, every three years for abdominal aortic aneurysms 30-39 mm in diameter, annually for aneurysms 40-44 mm, and every six months for aneurysms >45 mm, taking into account life expectancy, suitability for future repair, and patient preferences.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with small abdominal aortic aneurysms who are either not expected to reach the diameter threshold for repair within their life expectancy, or are unfit for repair, or prefer conservative management, should be considered for discontinuation of surveillance.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: All patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm should receive cardiovascular risk factor management with smoking cessation\*, blood pressure control\*, statin and antiplatelet therapy\*, and lifestyle advice (including exercise and healthy diet).

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with a small abdominal aortic aneurysm are recommended to stop smoking and should receive help to do this, to reduce the abdominal aortic aneurysm growth rate and risk of rupture.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Having a small abdominal aortic aneurysm is not a contraindication to using Fluoroquinolone antibiotics.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Restricting exercise or sexual activity in patients with small abdominal aortic aneurysms\* is not indicated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Men with an asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm < 55 mm are not recommended for elective repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Women with an asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm < 50 mm are not recommended for elective repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Men with an abdominal aortic aneurysm >55 mm should be considered for elective repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Women with an abdominal aortic aneurysm >50 mm may be considered for elective repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with small abdominal aortic aneurysms showing rapid growth (>10 mm/year) should be considered for re-measurement of the aneurysm diameter as the first measure.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm who have reached the diameter threshold for repair, but who initially are deemed unfit for repair should be considered for continued surveillance, referral to other specialists for optimisation of their fitness status and then reassessment.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Prior to abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, routine screening of the entire aorta, access and femoropopliteal arteries should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Prior to endovascular abdominal aortic repair, detailed pre-operative procedure planning with computer tomography angiography, including the use of a dedicated post-processing software analysis, should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with pre-operative cardiac work up, coronary revascularisation in patients with stable coronary artery disease, is not indicated prior to abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with poor functional capacity (defined as metabolic equivalents < 4) or with significant clinical risk factors (unstable angina, decompensated heart failure, severe valvular disease, and significant dysrhythmias), are recommended to be referred for cardiac work up and optimisation prior to elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients on dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention, delaying abdominal aortic aneurysm repair until after reduction to monotherapy may be considered. Conversely, performing endovascular aortic repair under dual antiplatelet therapy may be considered if repair cannot be postponed.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Assessment of pre-operative lung function by measuring forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) or forced vital capacity (FVC) is not indicated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with risk factors for pulmonary complications or a recent decline in respiratory function should be referred for respiratory work up and optimisation prior to elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Assessment of pre-operative kidney function by measuring serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is recommended prior to elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, especially in patients with renal impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate < 30 mL/min/1. 73 m^2).

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with renal impairment should be adequately hydrated before elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Assessment of pre-operative nutritional status by measuring serum albumin should be considered prior to elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, with an albumin level of < 2. 8 g/dL as the threshold for pre-operative correction.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Routine screening for asymptomatic carotid stenosis and routine prophylactic carotid intervention for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis prior to abdominal aortic aneurysm repair is not indicated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and a concomitant symptomatic (within the last six months) 50-99% carotid stenosis, carotid intervention before elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair is recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Initiation of beta blockers is not recommended prior to abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients undergoing elective abdominal aortic aneurysms repair should start statin treatment pre-operatively (ideally at least four weeks before surgery) and continue indefinitely post-operatively.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients undergoing elective open or endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair should be considered for continuation of established monotherapy with aspirin or thienopyridines (e. g. , clopidogrel) during the peri-operative period.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients undergoing elective abdominal aortic aneurysms repair are not recommended to be on dual therapy or oral anticoagulants during the peri-operative period.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: All patients undergoing open or endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair should receive peri-operative systemic antibiotic prophylaxis.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients undergoing elective open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair may be considered for peri-operative epidural analgesia or catheter based continuous wound analgesia, to maximise pain relief and minimise early post-operative complications.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients undergoing elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair may be considered for locoregional anaesthesia in preference to general anaesthesia.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Intra-operative use of cell salvage and re-transfusion should be considered during open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: In elective open or endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair intra-operative administration of intravenous heparin (50 - 100 IU/kg) is recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Intra-operative use of activated clotting time (ACT) may be considered during open and endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, to measure the effect of heparin in the individual patient and guide additional heparin administration.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: All patients undergoing elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and deemed at risk of post-operative venous thromboembolism should be considered for thromboprophylaxis.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, routine use of antimicrobial coated grafts to prevent aortic graft infection is not recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, the choice of a midline vs. transverse or transperitoneal vs. retroperitoneal abdominal incision should be considered based on surgeon preference and patient factors.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Reconstruction of the left renal vein after its division during open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair may be considered if important collaterals have been sacrificed.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, it is recommended to perform the proximal anastomosis as close as possible to the renal arteries to prevent later aneurysm development in the remaining infrarenal aortic segment.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, it is recommended to preserve the blood flow to at least one internal iliac artery to reduce the risk of buttock claudication and colonic ischaemia.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: In open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair routine re-implantation of the inferior mesenteric artery is not indicated but should be reserved for selected cases of suspected insufficient pelvic organ perfusion and the risk of colonic ischaemia.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, prophylactic use of mesh reinforcement of midline laparotomies should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, device selection should be considered based on aorto-iliac anatomy and the availability of unbiased long term durability data.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair outside the manufacturers Instruction for Use is not recommended in the elective setting.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For newer generations of stent grafts for abdominal aortic aneurysm treatment based on existing platforms, such as low profile devices, long term follow up in prospective registries is recommended, to ensure device performance and procedural durability through 10 years.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: New techniques and concepts for abdominal aortic aneurysm treatment are not recommended to be used routinely in clinical practice and should only be used within the framework of studies approved by research ethics committees, until adequately evaluated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysms repair, the choice of percutaneous access or cut down should be considered based on patient factors and operator preferences.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysms repair by a percutaneous approach, ultrasound guidance is recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, preservation of large accessory renal arteries (>4 mm) or those that supply a significant portion of the kidney (> 1/3) should be considered, however without compromising adequate sealing.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, routine pre-emptive embolisation of accessory renal arteries is not indicated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing endovascular repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm, routine pre-emptive embolisation of the inferior mesenteric artery, lumbar arteries, and non-selective aneurysm sac embolisation is not indicated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For most patients with suitable anatomy and reasonable life expectancy, endovascular repair should be considered the preferred treatment modality for elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For most patients with long life expectancy, open surgical repair should be considered as the preferred treatment modality for elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with limited life expectancy, elective abdominal aortic aneurysm repair is not recommended, either open or endovascular repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Laparoscopic abdominal aortic aneurysm repair is not recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: All patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing open surgical repair and high risk patients undergoing endovascular repair are recommended to have early post- operative monitoring in an intensive care or high dependency unit.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with a suspected ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm should undergo prompt imaging of the whole abdominal aorta and of the access vessels with computed tomography angiography.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: After endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm rupture into the inferior vena cava, subsequent endovascular closure of the aortocaval fistula may be considered in the presence of an endoleak associated with increased cardiac output, heart failure, or pulmonary embolisation.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, a policy of permissive hypotension is recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing endovascular repair of a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, local anaesthesia should be considered as the anaesthetic modality of choice, whenever tolerated by the patient.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Haemodynamically unstable patients with a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing open or endovascular repair may be considered for aortic balloon occlusion under fluoroscopy guidance to obtain proximal control.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients undergoing endovascular repair for a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm may be considered for a bifurcated device, in preference to an aorto-uni-iliac device, whenever anatomically suitable.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients undergoing endovascular repair for a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm in whom imaging was performed during permissive hypotension, should be considered for stent graft oversizing of up to 30%.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: In ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, intra-operative administration of systemic anticoagulation with heparin should be considered once the rupture bleeding has been controlled.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm should be considered for post-operative deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis with low molecular weight or unfractionated heparin unless there are signs of ongoing bleeding or of a clinically significant coagulopathy.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: **Selection of patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm for palliation based entirely on scoring systems or solely on advanced age is not recommended. **

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm and suitable anatomy endovascular repair is recommended as the first line treatment option.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: After open or endovascular treatment for a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, post-operative monitoring of intra-abdominal pressure is recommended for early diagnosis and management of intra-abdominal hypertension or abdominal compartment syndrome.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with abdominal compartment syndrome after open or endovascular treatment of a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm should be treated with decompressive laparotomy.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: In the management of open abdomen following decompression for abdominal compartment syndrome after open or endovascular treatment of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, a vacuum assisted closure system with mesh mediated traction and early abdominal closure should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing open or endovascular treatment for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm in whom colonic ischaemia is suspected, flexible sigmoidoscopy should be considered, to confirm the diagnosis.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with a symptomatic non-ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm may be considered for a brief period of rapid assessment and optimisation followed by urgent repair under optimal conditions (ideally during working hours).

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients operated on for an abdominal aortic aneurysm should receive post-operative cardiovascular risk management including statin therapy, antiplatelet medication, and blood pressure control.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients operated on for an abdominal aortic aneurysm with new onset or worsening of lower limb ischaemia are recommended immediate evaluation of graft related problems, such as limb kinking or occlusion.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients treated by endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair who present with asymptomatic non-obstructive mural thrombus formation limited to the main body of stent graft, intervention or escalation of antithrombotic therapy is not indicated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients treated by endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair who present with symptomatic, evolving, or haemodynamically significant thrombus formation inside the stent graft may be considered for individual intervention or escalation of antithrombotic therapy.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with aortic graft or stent graft infection should be considered for radical treatment with complete graft or stent graft explantation as first line treatment. **Class** IIa

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: In patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm after endovascular repair and suspected aortoenteric fistula, an emergency computed tomography angiography or endoscopy should be considered, in order to confirm the diagnosis and guide further treatment. **Class** IIa

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing complete explantation of an infected aortic graft or stent graft, extra-anatomic reconstruction may be considered an alternative repair modality in frail patients, in cases with extensive infections, or with graft enteric fistula.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For selected high risk patients with aortic graft or stent graft infection, conservative and/or palliative options should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For selected high risk patients with an isolated (localised) aortic graft or stent graft infection, less radical options than radical explantation, may be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with aorta or graft enteric fistula, adjuvant antifungal therapy should be considered, until fungal infection has been properly investigated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients treated for aortic graft or stent graft infection deemed at high risk of re-infection or when complete graft removal is not achieved, long term culture specific antibiotic therapy should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with an aortic prosthesis presenting with gastrointestinal bleeding, prompt assessment to identify a possible graft enteric fistula is recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with graft enteric fistula and bleeding, staged endovascular stent grafting as a bridge to open surgery may be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing open repair of graft enteric fistula, assessment and management of the enteric defect by a gastrointestinal surgeon should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients treated for abdominal aortic aneurysm who are distressed by post-operative new onset sexual dysfunction, referral to specialised teams should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with para-anastomotic aneurysm formation after previous abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, infection as the underlying cause should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with non-infectious para-anastomotic aneurysm formation after previous abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, endovascular repair should be considered preferentially.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with Type 1 endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair are recommended for prompt re-intervention to achieve a seal, primarily by endovascular means.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with compromised sealing zones\* without visible endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair may be considered for intervention to improve the seal, primarily by endovascular means.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a compromised proximal seal\* after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, proximal extension with fenestrated and branched devices should be considered in preference to other endovascular techniques.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For selected patients with a compromised proximal seal\* after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, elective open conversion may be considered as an alternative to complex endovascular interventions, provided the surgical risk is acceptable.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Secondary intervention for a Type 2 endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair should only be considered in the presence of significant aneurysm sac growth (> 10 mm compared with baseline or with the smallest diameter during follow up using the same imaging modality and measurement method), primarily by endovascular means, provided alternative causes including Type 1 or 3 endoleaks have been excluded.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with persistent aneurysm growth after endovascular aneurysm repair should be considered for secondary intervention to treat Type 2 endoleak using endovascular means with coiled trajectory planning are superior to standard techniques. Different embolic agents can be used, with the most frequent being coils of different types, alone or in combination with liquid embolic agents (ethylene vinyl alcohol). While the latter seems more effective, the actual value in arresting growth and preventing rupture remains unclear. A recent publication about the safety and efficacy of transarterial liquid embolisation, noted that up to one quarter of patients suffered peri-operative complications and the endoleak was eliminated in less than half. A recent publication suggests that treatment success can be significantly improved by using intra-operative CUS combined with cone beam CT for guidance during translumbar embolisation.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with Type 3 endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, prompt re-intervention is recommended, primarily by endovascular means.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with significant aneurysm sac growth (>10 mm compared with baseline or with the smallest diameter during follow up using the same imaging modality and measurement method) after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, without visible endoleak on standard imaging, should be considered for further diagnostic evaluation with alternative imaging modalities to exclude the presence of an occult endoleak or infection.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with significant aneurysm sac growth (> 10 mm compared with baseline or with the smallest diameter during follow up using the same imaging modality and measurement method) after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, without visible endoleak after multimodality imaging, should be considered for stent graft relining or conversion to open surgical repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients who have undergone open surgical repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm may be considered for imaging follow up of the entire aorta and peripheral arteries every five years.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients who have undergone endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair are recommended early post-operative imaging (within 30 days) using computed tomography angiography, to assess the presence of endoleak, component overlap and sealing zone length.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients who have been stratified as low risk of complications\* based on early post-operative computed tomography angiography should be considered for low frequency imaging follow up during the first five years.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients who have undergone endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair are recommended for long term imaging follow up (regardless of initial risk stratification), to detect late complications and identify late device failure and disease progression.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with complex abdominal aortic aneurysms may be considered for elective repair at a diameter of 55 mm in men and 50 mm in women, taking into account fitness for repair, aneurysm anatomy, and patient preferences.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing endovascular repair of complex abdominal aortic aneurysms, consideration should be given to limiting the aortic coverage to reduce the risk of spinal cord ischaemia, however without compromising the proximal sealing zone. |

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: During endovascular aortic repair of complex abdominal aortic aneurysms, the use of intra-operative image fusion should be considered, to reduce radiation exposure, contrast volume, and operating time.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: During endovascular repair of complex abdominal aortic aneurysms, the use of on table cone beam computed tomography imaging for completion control may be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm and standard surgical risk, open or endovascular repair should be considered based on patient fitness, anatomy, and patient preference.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm and high surgical risk, endovascular repair with fenestrated and branched technologies should be considered as first line therapy.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Endovascular repair for a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm using parallel graft techniques should only be considered as an option in the emergency setting, or as a bailout, and ideally be restricted to 2 chimneys.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm, use of new techniques and concepts is not recommended in routine clinical practice and should be limited to studies approved by research ethics committees, until adequately evaluated.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Hybrid repair, by means of visceral and renal artery re-routing (bypassing) combined with endovascular exclusion of the aneurysm, is not recommended as the first line treatment for complex abdominal aortic aneurysm.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing open repair of a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm with a suprarenal clamp time > 25 minutes, cold renal perfusion should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing endovascular repair of a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm a strategy to preserve renal function by dose reduction of iodine contrast media, withdrawal of nephrotoxic drugs and ensuring adequate hydration should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For endovascular repair of a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm, preservation of large accessory renal arteries (>4 mm) should be considered.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing open or endovascular repair of a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm, a policy of reactive (rescue) cerebrospinal fluid drainage may be considered preferable over routine prophylactic cerebrospinal fluid drainage.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a ruptured complex abdominal aortic aneurysm (or who are deemed urgent for any other reason), open surgical repair or endovascular repair (with off the shelf branched stent graft, physician modified endograft, in situ fenestrations, or parallel grafts) should be considered based on patient status, anatomy, and patient preferences.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: After endovascular treatment for a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm, long term imaging surveillance is recommended; with computed tomography angiography within 30 days and one year and thereafter individualised.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: After endovascular treatment for a complex abdominal aortic aneurysm, duplex ultrasound surveillance may be considered as an alternative to continued computed tomography angiography surveillance after the first post-operative year in selected patients.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients deemed at risk of bridging stent patency failure after endovascular treatment for complex abdominal aortic aneurysm may be considered for dual antiplatelet therapy in the early post-operative period.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with target vessel obstruction after complex abdominal aortic aneurysm repair should be considered for prompt evaluation for possible revascularisation.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with an iliac artery aneurysm (common iliac artery, internal iliac artery, and external iliac artery, or combination thereof), imaging surveillance using ultrasound should be considered; every three years for aneurysms 20-24 mm in diameter, every two years for aneurysms 25 — 29 mm in diameter, and yearly for aneurysms ≥ 30 mm, taking into account life expectancy, suitability for future repair, concomitant aortic dilatation, and patient preferences.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an iliac artery aneurysm (common iliac artery, internal iliac artery, and external iliac artery, or combination thereof) should be considered for elective repair at a diameter of 40 mm.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: The choice of surgical technique for iliac artery aneurysm repair should be considered based on individual patient and lesion characteristics.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Preserving blood flow to at least one internal iliac artery during open surgical and endovascular repair of iliac artery aneurysms is recommended.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients undergoing common iliac artery aneurysm repair in whom internal iliac artery embolisation or ligation is necessary, occlusion of the proximal main stem of the vessel is recommended if technically feasible, to preserve the distal collateral circulation to the pelvis.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: The diagnosis of a mycotic abdominal aortic aneurysm is recommended to be based on a combination of clinical, laboratory, and imaging parameters.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with a suspected mycotic abdominal aortic aneurysm are recommended for treatment with intravenous antibiotics; empirical antibiotic treatment should cover Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella species, and as soon as cultures have been obtained, treatment should be targeted empirically according to the results of cultures. Continued empirical treatment in cases with negative cultures.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Prompt surgical treatment of mycotic abdominal aortic aneurysms is recommended, irrespective of aneurysm size, due to the high rupture risk.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with mycotic abdominal aortic aneurysms are recommended to be referred to high volume vascular surgical centres, for multidisciplinary management.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: The choice of surgical technique for the treatment of a mycotic abdominal aortic aneurysm should be considered based on individual patient and lesion characteristics.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients who have undergone mycotic abdominal aneurysm repair should be considered for an individualised postoperative antibiotic regimen and surveillance strategy, based on patient factors, microbiology, and the surgical technique used.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: When measuring the diameter of inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysms to determine the indication for repair, the peri-aortic inflammation or wall oedema should not be included.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: All patients with symptomatic inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysms should be considered for medical anti-inflammatory treatment, with corticosteroids being the initiation therapy of choice.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm should be considered for repair at an aneurysm diameter of 55 mm, with endovascular repair in preference to open surgical repair if the anatomy is suitable.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an uncomplicated\* penetrating aortic ulcer, isolated dissection, or intramural haematoma of the abdominal aorta should be considered for conservative management with best medical treatment and continued surveillance.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with a pseudoaneurysm or complicated\* penetrating aortic ulcer, isolated dissection, or intramural haematoma on the abdominal aorta should be considered for surgical treatment, preferably by endovascular means.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Early surgical treatment (open or endovascular) may be considered for penetrating aortic ulcer and saccular abdominal aortic aneurysms, with a lower diameter threshold for elective repair than for a standard fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and concomitant cancer are not recommended a different treatment threshold (diameter) for prophylactic aneurysm repair compared with other cancer, including cases of synchronous cancer.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with a large or symptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm with an indication for repair and concomitant malignancy should be considered for a staged surgical approach, with endovascular repair first, to allow for treatment of the malignancy with minimal delay.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with concomitant cancer should be considered for prolonged low molecular weight heparin prophylaxis for up to four weeks after abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm with a suspected underlying genetic cause, such as early onset (< 60 years) or positive family history of aneurysmal disease, or with physical features associated with monogenetic syndromes, are recommended for genetic evaluation.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Referral to a multidisciplinary aortic team at a highly specialised centre is recommended to manage patients with aortic disorder suspected to have an underlying genetic cause.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Patients with vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome are recommended prophylactic treatment with celiprolol.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: In young patients with suspected connective tissue disorders and an abdominal aortic aneurysm, open surgical repair is recommended as first option.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with abdominal aortic aneurysms with an underlying genetic cause, the threshold diameter for considering repair should be individualised, depending on the underlying genetics and anatomy.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Shared decision making should be facilitated during conversations around abdominal aortic aneurysm screening, surveillance and the management of large asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysms being considered for repair.

guideline_name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
rec_text_verbatim: Use of decision support tools to assist patients in their decisions about the management of abdominal aortic aneurysms being considered for repair should be considered.
